newsitem.title: USA: CME Nov lumber futures tumble again into close.
newsitem.headline: CME Nov lumber futures tumble again into close.

text.p: November CME lumber futures had recovered to near-previous levels on short covering but fell again late on a combination of new selling, bear spreading and fund liquidation. Other months ended higher on the short covering and spread action, traders said.

Futures were under initial pressure in an expanded daily trading limit of $15.00 per tbf before meeting support. Two consecutive days of limit losses in November and January contracts resulted in the expanded limits, but prices recovered as the market appeared oversold following the recent sharp setback, traders said.

Cash markets have topped and usually break seasonally going into the fall and winter holiday period before rising again early the next year. This seasonal trend prompted much of the spread action, they said.
"Really there is no price right now -- the market is really soft in fir, pine and spruce," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.
Lumber closed $7.90 per tbf lower to $3.10 higher with only November off at $343.10 per tbf. January led back months higher at $343.10 per tbf.
